summary: node1 now has a persistent firewalld policy permitting SSH and TCP 8080 while rejecting unrelated inbound TCP connections. The policy survived a verified node reboot; services recovered automatically, protected data remained unchanged, and all test artifacts were removed.
actions_performed: Kept the existing RHEL 10 release, kernel, and supported firewalld/nftables stack.
Added persistent TCP 8080 access and retained SSH access.
Removed the unrelated Cockpit and DHCPv6-client inbound allowances.
Verified TCP 22 and 8080 are accepted while TCP 9090 and 18081 are rejected.
Restarted node1 exactly once and verified persistence and recovery.

evidence.requirement: Persistent firewall permits only SSH and TCP 8080 for ordinary inbound TCP access
evidence.summary: Permanent and runtime public-zone configuration contains SSH and 8080/tcp; effective nftables rules accept ports 22 and 8080 and reject unmatched inbound traffic.

evidence.requirement: Allowed and unrelated inbound connection behavior
evidence.summary: Isolated-client tests showed the intended policy transition and, after reboot, accepted TCP 22/8080 while explicitly rejecting live listeners on TCP 9090/18081.

Healthy pre-restart state and boot ID were captured, reboot was acknowledged, boot ID changed from 180a78a0-8a84-45ff-82f1-cd734208a369 to 414c44e5-487e-4d0b-a3e4-8c7bc8be4de9, and service/configuration/behavior recovery was verified.

evidence.requirement: Operating system, kernel, administrative access, protected data, and cleanup preserved
evidence.summary: RHEL 10.0 and kernel 6.12.0-55.9.1.el10_0 remain installed; sshd is enabled, active, and listening; protected-file checksums are unchanged; there are no failed units or temporary test artifacts.
